title: verify_test_env C3 migrates BPM_DB_URL while C4 verifies BPM_TEST_DB_URL — C3 can report PASS against an unmigrated test database
symptom: In a single `zig build test-env-verify` run, C3 (`zig build migrate`) reported PASS while C4 (schema baseline) reported FAIL with `public.schema_migrations has 106 rows for schema_name='public', but migrations/ contains 108 *.sql files (delta = -2)`. The two missing migrations were 1136_iss0149_exp301_effects_outbox_tenant_scope.sql and 1137_iss0156_entity_instance_projection_backfill.sql. Running `zig build migrate` with BPM_DB_URL explicitly pointed at the test database applied both and turned C4 green.
root_cause_analysis: check_migrate() (C3) runs a bare `zig build migrate`, whose DB resolution prefers BPM_DB_URL (the development database). check_schema_baseline() (C4) always verifies BPM_TEST_DB_URL (the test database) — see tools/verify_test_env.py:285-303 vs :238-262. When BPM_DB_URL and BPM_TEST_DB_URL point at different databases (the normal configuration: .env sets bpm_dev and bpm_test separately), C3 migrates a database that C4 never inspects and that no integration test uses. C3's PASS therefore carries no information about the database the tests will actually run against, and its remedy string ('resolve the migration failure above') misdirects, because no migration failed — the migration targeted the wrong database.
impact: C3's role in the Infrastructure Health Checklist (docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md §3) is to establish that the database the integration tests will use is fully migrated. As implemented it can certify a database no test touches. This is a false green on a hard gate: TEST-RUNNER may be cleared to run against an unmigrated test database, and the resulting failures surface later as confusing schema errors rather than as an environment check failure. It also weakens C4's diagnostic value, since the operator sees a PASS and a FAIL that appear to contradict each other.
acceptance_criteria: C3 migrates the same database C4 verifies, or C3 runs migrate once per distinct configured database URL
A test database that is behind migrations/ causes C3 itself to FAIL, not only C4
C3's remedy text distinguishes 'migration failed' from 'migration targeted a different database'
The fix is verified by leaving the test DB deliberately behind by one migration and confirming C3 reports FAIL
related: ISS-0152 / GH #484 — this was found while verifying that issue's premise
ISS-0140 / GH #443 — prior C3 false-positive fix in the same function
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only'. Not fixed in WF03-ISS-0152-20260807: it did not block that run's acceptance criteria, and changing a gate's own definition belongs in its own run with its own review, per 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures'.
